pr_title: bn_ppc.c: Fix build failure on AIX with XLC/XLCLANG
pr_body:
These compilers define _ARCH_PPC64 for 32 bit builds
so we cannot depend solely on this define to identify
32 bit build.

Fixes #17087
pr_comments: This pull request is ready to merge
Merged to master and 3.0 branches. Thank you for the review.

issue_context.title: [3.0.0] Build failures on AIX 7.2 XLC/XLCLANG 16.1 32bit
issue_context.body:
Hey guys,
Seeing similar linking errors using both xlc and xlclang compiler frontends for 32bit. The undefined symbols differ between them though. I've set `-bnoquiet` to get more info.
64bit builds and tests fine. Both run on the same machines.
Is this another LIBPATH issue? It's just set to the system default. 
If so, what's changed since 1.1.1 that requires it to be set explicitly?

A small point: you want to know what macros the compiler pre-defines for 32-bit builds, right?  That's probably not what you got with `xlclang++ -qshowmacros -E test.c`, you probably need to stick in `-q32` in that command...  also, and I'm not sure if this is relevant in this case or not, but generally speaking, you should probably use `xclang` rather than `xclang++`, since it's the former that you use to compile OpenSSL.

Now, to the architecure macros; the trouble with macros like `_ARCH_PPC64` is that they are largely compiler specific...  some compilers try hard to be compatible with other compilers (clang, for example, tries hard to be gcc compatible in many ways), but other than that, there are varieties in what macros they predefine.
https://sourceforge.net/p/predef/wiki/Architectures/#powerpc is a compilation of macros that some compilers support.  Looking there, you can for example see that gcc has another set of macros, all starting with `__powerpc` or `__PPC`.
This goes to show that you will have to look at more alternatives than macros that have `ARCH` in their names...  try to grep for `powerpc` or `PPC` in the `xclang -q32 -qshowmacros` output and see what you get.

I hope all this advice gets you further in figuring this out.

> Another issue I've found is that somebody moved `ppc_arch.h` from `<src-root>/crypto` to `<src-root>/include/crypto` but never updated the include statements to use angle brackets (system path) instead of double quotes (relative path).

That's not relevant.  The `-I` values on the compiler command lines form a search path that's used for *both* system path and "relative path" header searches.  You'll probably find this confirmed in your compiler manual.
We only use angle brackets on the `openssl/{name}.h` header files (i.e. what's in `<src-root>/include/openssl`), because when OpenSSL is installed (from a source build or from a vendor package), those are the ones that become system headers.
